newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-SGI sees volume product shipments.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-SGI sees volume product shipments.

text.p: Silicon Graphics Chairman and CEO Edward McCracken expects all but the latest of the company's sweeping new product lines to be in full production by the end of the current quarter.

The latest product, Octane workstations, will begin production in the March quarter and reach volume shipments in the June quarter, said McCracken, adding that Silicon Graphics executives see a $1 billion a year market for Octane beginning in the company's 1998 fiscal year.
McCracken also said in an interview he would not rule out support one day for Microsoft's Windows NT system.

"I won't preclude anything," said McCracken, when asked about industry analyst's concerns that a number of new independent software vendors with hot products favored Windows NT over Unix platforms such as those Silicon Graphics uses.

"Our purpose as a company is to provide products that unleash the power of human creativity and insight and we'll use whatever tools we can to implement those kind of products," he said, adding he would neither rule out support for Windows NT, nor commit to supporting it at this time.
He said SGI's entry-level O2 machines can outperform more expensively-priced PCs that use Intel chips.

"The O2 is less expensive and has three to four times the performance for any kind of 3-D graphics applications," said McCracken, adding Silicon Graphics' powerful higher-end Octane workstations have technology that can connect a computer's internal devices at 10 times the speed of a top-end PC.
Some analysts said they expect personal computers to start eroding the low-end of the Silicon Graphics market just the same, but SGI executives said they are not standing still.
McCracken said the company is returning to more of an even keel after the difficulties it encountered starting up manufacturing of its broad new product line.

"We're in a rapidly changing business," McCracken said. "The execution in the middle of such rapid change is sometimes a little unpredictible, but we think we're on top of the real issues facing the company."
For example, he said all of the four product lines the company unveiled last October should be in full production by the end of the current quarter at the end of March.
"All of our products should ship in real volume this quarter except the Octane, which should be in limited production," he said. "We should be in full volume on Octane in the June quarter."

The Silicon Graphics chief executive declined, however, to address analyst estimates for the third fiscal quarter, or for the fiscal year to June 30. Consensus earnings estimates are for SGI to earn $0.29 a share in its third quarter and $0.91 per share for the fiscal year, according to First Call.

"Certainly it would be a little easier if we did these products one at a time," he said. "Doing four products at the same time, which is what we did a quarter ago, is not something I would like to make a standard practice."
McCracken declined to discuss Silicon Graphics' plans for new processors, but said its new machines will accept them.
